newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges tumble under selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges tumble under selling pressure.

text.p: European fuel oil markets were rocky on Wednesday, with barge prices buffeted by aggressive selling that dominated thin business, traders said.

High sulphur barge offers started at $86 but quickly fell. Two deals were heard done at $83, another at $82.50 fob ARA before the low was set with a $79.50 sale for April late in the afternoon. Barge swaps tumbled in response.
May material was priced at $82.50 fob.
"Its because nothing was happening, it was dead, and the sellers wanted to see some bids come in," said one trader.
"It was a quiet and rather strange market today," said another trader, pointing out that total volume appeared to be below 10,000 tonnes.
Cargo markets were overshadowed by the barge market's behaviour, though traders said the overall tone was softer.

A trader bought Scandinavian high sulphur cracked late on Tuesday at $74.50, with the material's final destination unknown. Otherwise, high sulphur cargoes were better bid than offered, dealers reported.
Low sulphur cargo markets were quiet.
